neighbours.label: evidence pointing to a conclusion: 'point(s)' / ' to' in 'the evidence points to', 'lends weight to', 'evidence to suggest'
fire: Taken together, the fossils point to a much wetter climate in that period.
Early results lend support to the view that the drug slows the disease.
Everything we have found so far points to a fault in the wiring.
The survey data lend weight to claims that rents are rising fastest in the north.
Several clues point to the gardener as the author of the letters.
Researchers say there is growing evidence to suggest that the lake is warming.
The pattern of damage points to a fire that started in the kitchen.
These measurements lend credence to the theory of a hidden ocean.
quiet: Standing together, the tourists point at a much taller tower across the river.
Early results were sent to the board before the drug went on sale.
Everything we have found so far goes to a warehouse near the station.
The survey data were handed to officials in the north last week.
Several arrows point the way to the garden behind the church.
Researchers say they took the evidence to a laboratory by the lake.
The teacher points to a map that hangs in the kitchen.
These measurements were lent to a museum for the summer.

notes: Card: ' to' x11, ' point(s)' x7, ' lends' x2, all where evidence or findings indicate something; the output promotes ' evidence', ' findings', ' suggests'. Probes: evidential uses 0.50-0.67 (also 'signs point to' 0.53, 'findings point toward' 0.67); a guide pointing to a door 0.07; 'gave the keys to' 0.01.
